- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to counteract pessimism.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overreacts and overshoots; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.4) and price is trending down, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; add a slight upward bias (0.5–1.5%) to prevent premature decline.
- Model frequently underestimates short-term volatility in sentiment-heavy periods; increase forecast variance by 0.5–1.5% in days with sentiment >0.3.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to lag behind true price by 2–4 days; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead if sentiment is rising, or delay if sentiment is falling.
- When sentiment is flat or neutral (0.1–0.3), model often overfits recent history; apply smoothing filter or reduce weight on last 3–5 data points.
